mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized near -19 to -21 over the last four weeks after an initial decline, suggesting a plateau. This steady-state pattern implies the next four weeks will continue near current levels with no further deterioration, consistent with mean-reversion toward the recent average.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC oscillated between -18.6 and -21.3 over last four weeks without a clear trend
failure_condition: If mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below -21.3 (the lowest weekly value observed in the snapshot), the plateau hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in PARKS mobility from -26.1 to -32.4 over four weeks indicates reduced outdoor leisure activity, likely due to weather or seasonal shift, which may displace some recreation demand toward indoor retail, partially offsetting RETAIL_REC declines and pushing it modestly higher in the next 4 weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline in tandem with PARKS over the next two weeks rather than diverging upward, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained flat to slightly improving (-19.0 to -18.4) over the snapshot period, indicating stable commuting and travel patterns. If TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week from the t-0w level, it signals a renewed mobility restriction that would drag RETAIL_REC downward in the following weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week from the t-0w value of -18.4
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved slightly from -19.0 to -18.4 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: If TRANSIT drops sharply but RETAIL_REC does not decline in the subsequent two weeks, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of rising RESIDENTIAL (6.4 to 7.0) alongside falling WORKPLACES (-13.4 to -12.9, near flat but not recovering) suggests sustained at-home behavior that structurally suppresses out-of-home retail activity; their combined persistence predicts continued suppression of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 6.4 to 7.0 while WORKPLACES stayed near -13
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises above the last-28-day mean despite RESIDENTIAL staying elevated and WORKPLACES remaining suppressed, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous sharp decline in PARKS (-26.1 to -32.9) and dip in RETAIL_REC at t-1w (-21.3) suggests a coordinated restriction event (e.g., advisory or policy tightening) around that week. If such restrictions persist (indicated by PARKS staying below -30), RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed over the next four weeks relative to the prior period.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -30 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -32.9 at t-1w and stayed at -32.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS recovers above -28 within two weeks but RETAIL_REC fails to recover correspondingly, or if RETAIL_REC recovers despite PARKS staying depressed, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed relatively stable and mild (-11.6 to -13.9) compared to deeper RETAIL_REC declines, indicating essential-goods shopping is largely decoupled from discretionary retail behavior. This stability predicts GROCERY_PHARM will not meaningfully drive RETAIL_REC changes in the near term, so RETAIL_REC movement will be driven by other factors and is expected to remain flat to slightly negative over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM varied only 2.3 points across four weeks while RETAIL_REC varied more
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC moves sharply upward in the next week in correlation with changes in GROCERY_PHARM, the decoupling hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve (become less negative) simultaneously over the next week, this signals a synchronized return to commuting and office-based routines, which jointly drives higher incidental retail footfall near transit hubs and workplaces, raising RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: Both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by more than 2 points week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improved slightly from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the subsequent four weeks, the synchronized-commute mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The pronounced week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility (-28.7 to -32.9) between t-2w and t-1w coincides with a seasonal cooling or weather shift that reduces outdoor activity broadly, which in steady state also correlates with reduced casual retail visits, implying RETAIL_REC will continue a mild downward drift over the next two weeks mirroring the parks decline.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined by 4.2 points from t-2w to t-1w, the largest weekly drop in the snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks while PARKS continues its downward trajectory, the shared-seasonal-driver hypothesis is rejected.
